Where it began

Inderbir Singh Sodhi, better known as Ish, was born in Ludhiana, in India, on 31 October 1992. When he was four his family moved to Papatoetoe, in New Zealand, and he went to Papatoetoe High School.

He bowled right-arm leg spin and batted right-handed, and Northern Districts gave him his start in the 2012–13 season. He stayed with them for ten seasons, then moved to Canterbury for the 2022–2023 season. In 2018–19 no one in the Plunket Shield took more wickets: he had 36 in seven matches.

The player

His Test debut came on New Zealand's tour of Bangladesh in 2013. A year later, against Pakistan, he made 63, which was then the highest Test score by a New Zealand number ten. In 21 Tests between 2013 and 2024 he took 58 wickets at 43.10 with a best of 6 for 86. He made 561 runs at 20.78, with four fifties and a top score of 65, and held 11 catches.

His best Test came after four years away. Recalled for the tour of Pakistan in December 2022, he took his first five-wicket haul in Tests in the opening match and made his highest Test score, 65, in the same game. His best with bat and ball in one match is quite a way to say hello again.

What made him special

In the shorter game he was one of the best in the world. In January 2018 he rose from tenth to first in the T20 international bowling rankings, and a year earlier, for the Adelaide Strikers, he had taken 6 for 11 in 3.3 overs, among the best figures the Big Bash had seen. He was in New Zealand's squad that reached the final of the 2019 World Cup, and in their T20 World Cup squads in 2021 and 2024.

Test wickets came at a higher price. That is the leg-spinner's lot: some days the ball does the talking and some days the batters do. He kept tossing it up all the same, which is exactly what a leg-spinner is for.

Away from the middle

He took his leg breaks around the world, to the Big Bash, the Caribbean Premier League with the St Kitts & Nevis Patriots and the IPL with the Rajasthan Royals. In October 2025, against Australia, he played his 127th T20 international, more than any other New Zealand man had played.

And finally

In June 2023 Somerset brought him in for the Vitality Blast to fill a couple of gaps in the squad. He took three wickets in the final, and Somerset won it by 14 runs. As stopgaps go, it was a very good one.
